about: The logistics curriculum ATLAS's knowledge is organised by: six domains from fundamentals to advanced problem solving, plus the ATLAS project's own rules. Levels: 1 foundation, 2 intermediate, 3 advanced.

domains.title: Logistics and supply chain fundamentals
objectives: Tell logistics from supply chain management
Name the parties to a shipment and what each is responsible for
Use shipment, consignment, order, cargo and freight precisely
Explain inventory, warehousing, capacity and demand planning

domains.title: Transportation and freight
objectives: Compare air, ocean, road, rail and multimodal transport
Choose between FCL and LCL and the right equipment
Reason about transit time, lead time, cut-offs, routing and transshipment
Read a freight rate and its surcharges

domains.title: International trade and customs
objectives: Apply the Incoterms 2020 rules: costs, risk transfer, who clears
Know what each trade document proves
Explain HS classification, valuation, duties and clearance
Diagnose holds, inspections and discrepancies; know demurrage from detention
domains.note: Educational explanations. Country rules differ and change: a jurisdiction item names its country, its source and when it was last reviewed, and is never presented as current law beyond that.

domains.title: Shipment lifecycle and operational tracking
objectives: Follow a shipment from booking to proof of delivery
Use ETA, ETD, ATA, ATD and milestones correctly
Handle delays, missing updates, conflicting statuses and data freshness
Escalate and involve a person at the right point

domains.title: Performance, analytics and KPIs
objectives: Define each KPI with its formula, unit, aggregation, period, fields, exclusions and limits
Calculate KPIs exactly
Tell industry conventions from business definitions
Compare carriers fairly

domains.title: Advanced operational problem solving
objectives: Separate causal from correlational evidence
Diagnose documentation and customs exceptions
Plan recovery and alternatives
Prioritise by risk and impact
Say when the evidence is not enough

domains.title: ATLAS project rules
objectives: Know how this platform decides, writes and verifies
Never let a textbook definition override a verified project rule
domains.note: Business rules of this platform, each verifiable in the code it cites. Where a general definition differs, ATLAS shows both and says which one the platform applies.

review_statuses.unreviewed: written for ATLAS, not yet reviewed by a Mantrac subject-matter expert: shown, labelled as such
review_statuses.reviewed: checked by a reviewer; not yet approved as Mantrac's position
review_statuses.superseded: replaced by a newer item; kept for history, never answered as current
review_statuses.retired: withdrawn; kept for history, never answered

evidence_statuses.project_verified: states what this platform's code does; checkable in the cited file
evidence_statuses.source_cited: a real, checked source covers the topic; the text is ATLAS's own explanation, not a quotation
evidence_statuses.general_knowledge: widely taught logistics knowledge; no specific source checked
evidence_statuses.unverified: a claim not yet supported by a source; shown only with that label
